request: Can you help me find a light, sweet wine with some spice to have with dessert?
wines:
Wine 1: Moscato, US, $12. Tasting note: "Flowery and sweet through and through, this lighthearted dessert wine could also serve as apéritif as it's perfectly sippable, or as a pairing with something packed with spice, like enchiladas or red curry."
Wine 2: Riesling, France, $28. Tasting note: "Spice and cream dominate this attractive wine. With its full flavors of spice and pear, there is a also a hint of flower. An attractive wine that is developing quickly."
Wine 3: Muscat of Alexandria, Greece, $15. Tasting note: "This dessert wine offers rich aromas of spice, flowers and burnt orange/citrus, followed by opulent waves of honey, flowers and butterscotch. Pretty and a good pairing with cakes, fruit and cheeses."
Wine 4: Muscat, US, $13. Tasting note: "This has a sweet charm to it, with a rich lemon flavor. This would be fine as a light dessert wine with lemon cake."
Wine 5: Red Blend, Italy, $75. Tasting note: "This rich, amber colored dessert wine from Tuscany offers aromas of dried figs, nutmeg, clove sage and balsamic notes. The dense palate delivers maple syrup, candied fruit, dried apricots, honey and spice. It's concentrated and smooth with great length."

request: Can I get a bottle of sparkling wine that tastes like butter for under 15 euros to go with a cheese board?
wines:
Wine 1: Red Blend, US, $100. Tasting note: "There's magic in this 65% Petit Verdot and 35% Sangiovese combination. This shows concentrated cherry and kirsch aromas, touches of shiitake and porcini mushrooms and plenty of turned, wet earth aromas. The palate, framed by chalky tannins, offers more mushrooms and truffles in a black cherry-chocolate gravy, proving quite luxurious and interesting at once."
Wine 2: Garnacha, Spain, $7. Tasting note: "A perfectly solid Garnacha with pepper, bright red fruit and a touch of country style to the bouquet despite its pedestrian price. The palate is bright and tastes of plum and red berry, while the feel is good and the finish fruity and lively. What inexpensive red wine should be."
Wine 3: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $22. Tasting note: "This brisk and refreshing wine never saw a splinter of oak, so what stars are the pure, ripe flavors of tropical and citrus fruits, lemongrass, honey and a hint of white pepper. The acidity gives it a keen, clean finish. This would be great with everything from roast chicken to Vietnamese food."
Wine 4: Melon, France, $17. Tasting note: "From 40-year-old vines in a single vineyard, this rich wine is dense, aromatic and packed with concentrated fruit. Its citrus and crisp texture is balanced by the ripe green-plum and apple flavors. Drink this fine wine now."
Wine 5: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "This light, fruity wine does have tannins that give dryness along with mature berry fruit. Dried fruitcake flavors dominate and the wine will not age further. Drink now."

request: Hi, I am looking for a bottle of wine to drink tonight that tastes like red berries.
wines:
Wine 1: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $20. Tasting note: "A ripe, juicy and smoky wine that is already attractive to drink. It has soft tannins, ripe red berries with acidity and black currants at the end. Drink this fine wine from 2020."
Wine 2: Pinot Noir, France, $23. Tasting note: "This is a fruity, lightly structured wine. With perfumed red berries and tight acidity, it is all about fruitiness and freshness. It needs to fill out and to become as rich as its potential suggests. Drink from 2018."
Wine 3: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $9. Tasting note: "This is a full, fruity, rich and concentrated wine. It has bright red berries, some firm tannins and a good dense texture. It's also light and crisp, with acidity that cuts through the ripe fruitiness. Drink now through 2019."
Wine 4: Pinot Noir, France, $35. Tasting note: "This wine offers red berry fruits, the softest tannins and texture and an earthy, rustic aftertaste. Drink now."
Wine 5: Syrah, US, $38. Tasting note: "This is a soft, richly attractive red wine to drink now. It shows elaborate blackberry, cherry, currant, teriyaki beef, black pepper, anise and sandalwood flavors. An elegant mouthfeel, grows better as it breathes in the glass."

request: Can I try a sweet, strong, and cheap wine that goes down super easy and is something totally new for me?
wines:
Wine 1: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $18. Tasting note: "This is a smooth, impressively rich wine powered by silky tannins and ripe black fruits. The palate is intensely concentrated with a big, bold structure and a solid feel. It does need some aging, so drink from 2016."
Wine 2: Touriga Nacional, Portugal, $36. Tasting note: "Named after the barn owl (Tyto alba) that nests in the woods of the Lezirias estate, this has great tannins that give shape to the dense black fruits. With a powerful structure and so much of the Touriga Nacional perfumes, this is a wine for aging. Drink from 2018."
Wine 3: Touriga Nacional, Portugal, $36. Tasting note: "This 100% Touriga Nacional comes from the government-owned estate in the north of Tejo. Named after the barn owl that is found in the woods, the wine is structured with dense tannins as well as concentrated black fruits. It is balanced with its fruit and structure already working well together, but it will need time. Drink from 2019."
Wine 4: Fernão Pires, Portugal, $77. Tasting note: "This fine low-production wood-aged wine is almost Burgundian in its creamy richness. The toast is nicely judged giving a wine that has just enough acidity and has plenty of textured apple and grapefruit flavors. The wine is named after the year of the creation of the Companhia das Lezirias."
Wine 5: Castelão, Portugal, $18. Tasting note: "A serious and dense wine, this is rich and full of dark juicy fruit. It has plenty of structure of course, with its rich tannins and wood aging flavors right up front. The acidity is perfumed, underlining the ripe fruit. Drink this concentrated wine from 2018."

request: Can you help me find a sweet rosé wine that is nice and light?
wines:
Wine 1: Rosé, US, $10. Tasting note: "Pretty dark and full-bodied for a rosé, and too extracted and heavy in cherry-berry flavors to be considered elegant. It's almost a red wine you could drink at room temperature."
Wine 2: Rosé, France, $13. Tasting note: "A simple, fruity wine, this has light acidity and a touch of pepper at the end. It is a classic apéritif style of rosé."
Wine 3: Rosé, US, $12. Tasting note: "Just what you want in a rosé, at a good price. It's a robust wine, dryish and spicy, with a creamy mouthfeel framing pleasant raspberry, cherry, prosciutto and vanilla flavors."
Wine 4: Rosé, Italy, price unknown. Tasting note: "Here's a clean and well-balanced rosé with a fresh bouquet of fruity and floral aromas, followed by a crisp, tonic mouthfeel. This is exactly the kind of wine that is appropriate to serve at outdoor picnics or with friends at lunch. Very nice."
Wine 5: Touriga Nacional, Portugal, $11. Tasting note: "A soft, lightly sweet style of rosé, flavored with strawberries and a touch of caramel. Fresh, and flavorful, with balancing acidity, this is a good apéritif wine."

request: Can I get any safe bottle for a quiet night in that tastes like green apple and red berries, just something that cannot go wrong?
wines:
Wine 1: Rhône-style Red Blend, France, $33. Tasting note: "This is a supple, medium- to full-bodied red for drinking over the next few years. The plummy flavors are a bit earthy, dark and indistinct, but pleasant enough, and the wine's silky finish features a bright burst of red fruit."
Wine 2: Pinot Noir, France, $10. Tasting note: "This sophisticated and stylish Pinot Noir from the south of France was made a Burgundy producer. It has fine tannins, juicy red cherry-driven acidity and a warm, ripe aftertaste."
Wine 3: Merlot, US, $40. Tasting note: "Volatile aromas of cranberry, cherry and vanilla are followed by gritty lightly sweet cranberry and green-pepper flavors that show some astringency. The concentration seems lacking."
Wine 4: Austrian white blend, Austria, price unknown. Tasting note: "A field blend that's an Austrian tradition. It's a delicious, precocious mouth full with its apple acidity and fresh pink grapefruit flavors. It's a pleasure to drink now as an aperitif wine. Screwcap."
Wine 5: Austrian Red Blend, Austria, $36. Tasting note: "Red cherry fruit spiced by gentle white pepper notes makes for an enjoyable, fresh and joyful red. This combines the virtues of fruity, cherry-ish Zweigelt with the more sumptuous, fuller-bodied and spicy notions of Blaufränkisch. If you are new to Austrian reds, this pretty much is exquisite Burgenland in a glass."

request: Hi, I am looking for a sweet red wine that tastes like nuts.
wines:
Wine 1: Sherry, Spain, $18. Tasting note: "A smooth and coaxing Sherry with almond and dried fruit aromas that lead perfectly to toffee and almond flavors. There's more dryness than fruit here, with peanut brittle accents and then a long, smoky finish that doesn't lose focus. Graceful Oloroso, with a nice individual character."
Wine 2: Portuguese White, Portugal, $15. Tasting note: "A blend of Encruzado and Gouveio, this is a soft, creamy and fruity wine. It has no wood aging, emphasizing the ripe apricot and pear fruits. The aftertaste is crisp and bright."
Wine 3: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $20. Tasting note: "Dry and crisp, with good varietal flavors of citrus fruits and lemongrass. But this wine is also very potent in unripe, green notes that include the notorious feline component. That lowers the score."
Wine 4: Dolcetto, Italy, $20. Tasting note: "A simple but well made Dolcetto, with aromas of black cherry and stewed prunes followed by plum, licorice and graphite on the palate. It closes with a bitter almond note. This would work well with lasagna."
Wine 5: Norton, US, $30. Tasting note: "This Port-style dessert wine is lush in aromas and flavors of kirsch, fig, cooked plum, clove and coffee. A nice expression of the Norton grape, this is viscous and smooth, yet the finish brings a bite at the end."

request: Can you help me find a red wine that is not too heavy and is a really safe choice?
wines:
Wine 1: Merlot, Italy, $460. Tasting note: "A perfect wine from a classic vintage, the 2007 Masseto (100% Merlot from a 17-acre vineyard of the same name) opens with an unabashedly opulent bouquet of delicious blackberry, cherry, chocolate, vanilla, exotic spice and cinnamon. Masseto excels both in terms of quality of fruit and winemaking and delivers plush, velvety tannins and an extra long, supple finish. It will make a special and valuable collection to your cellar."
Wine 2: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $450. Tasting note: "This is the latest release of what has long been regarded as Portugal's iconic wine. And it is magnificent. The last vintage was the 2004 and the wait has now shown to be worthwhile. With its immense span and breadth of flavors and rich structure it is a superb manifestation of the great vineyards of the Douro Superior. Big bold fruits and acidity are matched by the tannins and concentration. Hold this for many years or at least wait until 2022."
Wine 3: Sangiovese, Italy, $550. Tasting note: "This gorgeous, fragrant wine opens with classic Sangiovese scents of violet, rose, perfumed red berry, new leather and a whiff of baking spice. The elegant, radiant palate delivers crushed Marasca cherry, ripe strawberry, cinnamon, black tea and a hint of pipe tobacco. Firm, ultrafine tannins and bright acidity offer an age-worthy structure and impeccable balance. It's already stunning but will evolve for decades. Drink 2020–2050."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $200. Tasting note: "Tasted in a flight of great and famous Napa wines, this Cardinale stood at the head of the pack. Starts with a very fine nose of cedar, cassis, ripe blackberries and violets, then turns dramatic and refined in the mouth. Shows vast depth and length, with the finish a full minute of sweet fruits and spices. Marvelous tannins, so plush and elegant, so powerful yet refined. The grapes hail from Mt. Veeder, Howell Mountain, Stags Leap and Oakville, and the blend contains 14% Merlot. As good as it is now, it will improve for at least eight years."
Wine 5: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $150. Tasting note: "This is a magnificently solid wine, initially even a bit severe. At this young stage, the tannins dominate, but it's also full of black fruit notes. Very dense and concentrated, this is a wine that's even better than the legendary 2005. The structure tells of its extraordinary aging potential: don't even attempt to drink this for 10 years."

request: Can you recommend a sparkling wine that tastes buttery, and costs under 25 euros?
wines:
Wine 1: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $15. Tasting note: "A very nice Cabernet at a great price for the quality. It's dry and smooth, with rich Napa tannins framing classic Cab flavors of blackberries, black currants, minerals and cedar. Tastes like it costs three times as much."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, US, $10. Tasting note: "Great price for a Chardonnay that tastes like it costs a lot more. Although it's unoaked, it's very rich in passionfruit, pineapple, peach and vanilla cream flavors, with a honeyed finish. Easy to find, with 5,000 cases produced."
Wine 3: Champagne Blend, US, $25. Tasting note: "From a bubbly specialist comes this fancy wine, a blend of 75% Pinot Noir and 25% Chardonnay. Has very forward fruity aromas that are a combo of both varietals. It’s a bit rough, as though the bubbles aren’t fine enough, but that’s comparing it to the best French vintage Champagne, which costs a whole lot more."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $25. Tasting note: "This wine is tight and tannic, with a rustic hint of leathery saddle and barnyard that makes it hard to highly recommend."
Wine 5: Red Blend, US, $28. Tasting note: "A pretty floral nose and appetizing, juicy flavors of jammy fruit should recommend this wine, but there's a bitterness on the midplate and finish that make the wine a touch too angular. Pair with food to even it out."

request: Can I get a popular white wine that everyone likes, not too heavy, with some spices and herbs?
wines:
Wine 1: Riesling, Austria, $25. Tasting note: "Lovely spiciness creeps into the lemon and tangerine zest that is on display here. Sprays of freshness and verve continue on the tight, linear palate that leaves a lasting impression of lip-smacking joy."
Wine 2: Syrah, US, $30. Tasting note: "There are swirls of faint red raspberry and black cherry in this wine, otherwise rich in ripe flavor and a taste of red licorice. Soft, satisfying and structured, it's got some weight to it, and some definite grip. A big wine for big meals."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, US, $54. Tasting note: "The Maritime bottling traditionally has represented some of the highest expressions of W.H. Smith's various Pinot Noirs. Gentle and yet complex, it opens with notes of raspberries and cherries accented with mushrooms and minerals. There's a deep, brooding earthiness, along with all sorts of spiced orange-rind and sandalwood notes. A great effort, and one of the best Pinots of the vintage. Drink now through 2020."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $35. Tasting note: "This combines fruity and savory aromas, with a rich but tannic texture and full body. Aroma recall black olive and cedar, while flavors focus on the fruit components. Everything is in place for an enjoyable, well-structured dinner wine."
Wine 5: St. Laurent, Austria, $44. Tasting note: "Dense and firm, dark plum fruits and tight tannins frame this wine against its fruits and spice flavors. Although it is not a heavyweight, the intensity of flavors more than compensates."

request: Can you suggest a popular red wine that everyone likes for a romantic dinner? We want something sweet and not too heavy, with flavors of spices and chocolate that we haven't tried before.
wines:
Wine 1: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $95. Tasting note: "This will impress red wine lovers with its sheer deliciousness. It offers waves of blackberry and blueberry jam, dark chocolate, anise and cedar wood flavors, leading to a long, spicy finish. It's a bit soft, which might limit ageability, but it is a lovely wine to drink over the next few years."
Wine 2: Zweigelt, Austria, $34. Tasting note: "An incredibly balanced wine where red cherry fruit marries with velvety tannins, medium body and clean-cut acidity and cinnamon hints in the background. This is an ideal, unobtrusive but delicious food wine that will perform no matter what."
Wine 3: Red Blend, US, $14. Tasting note: "This is a useful red wine for everyday drinking. Full-bodied and spicy, it offers plenty of berry, plum sauce and toasted wood flavors."
Wine 4: Merlot, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is a beautiful red wine to drink now for its rich, ripe flavors and overall balance. It's soft in acids and fine in tannins, offering heady waves of black cherries, currants and chocolate. Easy to find, with nearly 75,000 cases produced."
Wine 5: Primitivo, US, $28. Tasting note: "Sweet, but not very, and lacks the rich opulence you want in a dessert red wine. Shows plenty of raspberry and cherry flavor, but would benefit from greater intensity and sweetness."

request: Can you help me find a sweet rosé that tastes like peach and spices for under 15 euros to go with our fish dinner?
wines:

Wine 3: Nerello Mascalese, Italy, $16. Tasting note: "Here's an easy-going Nerello Mascalese-based rosé from Mt. Etna that offers piquant aromas of chopped mint, forest berry, gooseberry and cassis. The wine would pair well on informal occasions around a heaping bowl of fish soup."
Wine 4: Mourvèdre, US, $18. Tasting note: "A lovely rosé, dry and crisp, with peach skin, orange, strawberry and white pepper flavors, highlighted by brisk acidity. Would score higher if not for a certain heaviness."
Wine 5: Rosé, Italy, $15. Tasting note: "Here's a pale and luminous rosé from Southern Italy with a pinkish-peach color and delicate aromas of stone fruit, wild berries, white cherries and a touch of chopped mint or basil. The wine is tart but also slightly sweet in the mouth and there's a touch of bitter almond on the close."

request: I need a really nice bottle of rosé as a present, something juicy packed with red berry flavors, and price is not an issue at all.
wines:
Wine 1: Rosé, US, $150. Tasting note: "This is a beautiful, complex and complete wine, from the delicate, spiced raspberry aroma through the creamy, nuanced finish. Subtle but well-defined fruit flavors like white cherry and raspberry pulse across the palate, buoyed by an ultrafine effervescence and lively acidity. But the texture is smooth around the edges, lending a sense of extra depth and layering to this extraordinary bottle. Just coming into its own now, it will improve through at least 2020."
Wine 2: Rosé, France, $100. Tasting note: "This is a serious wine with a lighter brighter side. Its wood aging adds spice to the ripe red fruits and brings out the concentration and intensity. It is, in its way, an unexpected side of Provence rosé, emphasizing richness and complexity. But it all comes together: a fine wine that, after a year of aging, is ready to drink."
Wine 3: Rosé, France, $20. Tasting note: "This is one of the classics among Provence rosés. Produced from organically grown grapes and coming from an impressive red-wine producing estate east of Aix-en-Provence, the wine is structured and ageworthy with its blend that includes Cabernet Sauvignon. Rich and full of red fruits, the wine should be drunk from late 2017."
Wine 4: Rosé, US, $26. Tasting note: "This memorably beautiful and delicious wine is made from estate-grown Grenache. The grapes weren't designated for saignee, but rather picked specifically to make this tart and tangy expression of an inviting grape. Orange in color, almost like a beer, it's dry and sneakily succulent, with inviting floral aromas at its core and enough body to stay interesting as it develops."
Wine 5: Rosé, France, $20. Tasting note: "Coming from a remote estate on the edge of the Lubéron mountains in the north of Provence, this wine is impressively rich. It gains great concentration and structure from the Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah in the blend. Full of ripe red fruits, it is dense at the end."

request: Do you have a fresh white wine from a small maker that isn't too heavy and tastes like honey and butter?
wines:
Wine 1: Verdelho, US, $15. Tasting note: "With mouthwatering crispness and a pleasantly bitter, minerally tone, this fine, dry white wine is versatile at the table. It has savory flavors of citrus fruits, honeysuckle flowers and white pepper."
Wine 2: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "Drink this dryish wine with almost anything that calls for a light-bodied, crisp white, and don't worry about it. It has savory citrus flavors, with a pleasant hint of vanilla honey."
Wine 3: Chardonnay, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a basic white wine with a few quirks. It smells floral and appley, and tastes quite dry and a bit sharp while carrying a candylike marshmallow note."
Wine 4: Riesling, US, $9. Tasting note: "If you like your white wines fruity and sweet, this one's for you. It has pretty flavors of peaches, honey and spices."
Wine 5: White Blend, US, $21. Tasting note: "this full-bodied white wine stresses complexity, weight and viscosity. It smells like blanched almonds and candle wax, and tastes rich, almost heavy."

request: Can you help me find a light, sweet wine with some spice to have with dessert?
wines:
Wine 1: Merlot, US, $11. Tasting note: "As sweet as a dessert wine, with sugary raspberry, cherry and spice flavors."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, US, $9. Tasting note: "As sweet as a dessert wine, with simple pineapple jam flavors."
Wine 3: Muscat, US, $13. Tasting note: "This has a sweet charm to it, with a rich lemon flavor. This would be fine as a light dessert wine with lemon cake."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $27. Tasting note: "As sweet and sugary as a dessert wine, with watery berry flavors."
Wine 5: Müller-Thurgau, US, $12. Tasting note: "This simple and sweet wine has a light peach flavor with a sugary—not syrupy—finish. It might be a good wine to soak fruit in for a light dessert."

request: Do you have any sparkling wine that tastes like red berries and honey with a really creamy feel?
wines:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, France, $22. Tasting note: "This is a really fruity, really refreshing sparkling wine. It boasts apple, citrus and a touch of apricot flavors, as well as tight acidity. It is fragrant, pure and clean, and very fresh on the finish."
Wine 2: Champagne Blend, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "A lively, strawberry fruit-colored wine, light, soft and creamy. There is an attractive vibrant feel to the texture, with a hint of red berries, lifted by crisp acidity."
Wine 3: Sparkling Blend, France, $17. Tasting note: "Crisp, fresh sparkling wine, lightly creamy but more going towards green fruits, tight acidity. It doesn't need any bottle aging and really should be drunk in the next year to keep its essential freshness."
Wine 4: Gamay, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "Full-on banana aromas create a wine that tastes like an elderly nouveau. It does have some fruit and red cherries, but with a bitter edge, it really should have been drunk by now."
Wine 5: Chardonnay, US, $10. Tasting note: "This has creamy flavors of vanilla, honey, lime and orange."

request: I need a light sweet wine that tastes like plum to have at a barbecue.
wines:
Wine 1: Malbec, France, $15. Tasting note: "A big, burly wine with attractive tannins and rich plum and dark chocolate flavors. The wine is very accessible, ready to drink, a good value."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, France, $17. Tasting note: "Lightweight wine that seems somewhat dilute with flavors of green plums, bright acidity and a very soft texture."
Wine 3: Zinfandel, US, $24. Tasting note: "A thick, sweet and meaty dessert wine made from older vines, this offers a richness of Dr Pepper, baked plum and dried cherry."
Wine 4: Sangiovese, Italy, $62. Tasting note: "Ripe plum, mature black cherry, violet, clove, mocha, anise and grilled sage are just some of the sensations you'll find on this gorgeous wine alongside velvety tannins. It already has great depth but hold for more complexity. Drink 2017–2027."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $20. Tasting note: "Robust tannins and a nice character of plum, cherry and spice recommend this wine, though it has a slightly one dimensional simplicity to it. Pair with burgers and grilled lamb to bring out the good spice notes."

request: I need a sparkling wine that is sweet and tastes like peach with a crisp feel, to give as a present for a spicy curry, and the price does not matter.
wines:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, Italy, $34. Tasting note: "This straightforward sparkling wine offers peach aromas, with hints of roasted almond that carry over to the palate. This is refreshing, with a frothy texture and crisp acidity."
Wine 2: Sparkling Blend, US, $29. Tasting note: "Crisp peach and red-fruit flavors combine with vibrant acidity and energizing, fine bubbles to create a balanced and rich sparkling wine. A spicy, crisp fruit character lingers long on the finish."
Wine 3: Sparkling Blend, Italy, $30. Tasting note: "Made from Chardonnay and Pinot Nero, this sparkling wine offers peach and melon sensations along with notes of bitter almond. It has a vigorous palate with a crisp, clean finish. Pair it with appetizers, salami or cheese."
Wine 4: Sparkling Blend, Italy, $50. Tasting note: "This lovely sparkling wine is made with no dosage or added sugar. It offers scents of warm, just baked bread, citrus and roasted almond. The palate offers peach, apple, citrus and a hint of walnut along with crisp, clean acidity. It's smooth, with fine bubbles and a creamy texture."
Wine 5: Glera, Italy, $26. Tasting note: "Here's a simple sparkling wine that delivers subtle tones of peach and stone fruit with a thin and transparent appearance. This expression does a nice job of presenting sweet fruit tones against fresh acidity."

request: Can I try something new and get a dry rosé that is light, tastes like cherry, and feels really juicy?
wines:
Wine 1: Rosé, Portugal, $12. Tasting note: "This is an attractive, fruity, fresh rosé. It is dry but balances acidity and fruitiness with its sweet strawberry fruit and light touch of vanilla pod. Drink now."
Wine 2: Cabernet Franc, US, $13. Tasting note: "Quite dry yet intensely fruity, this has loads of fresh strawberry, red cherry and raspberry flavors. This finishes with a touch of sweet fruit and a subtle spray of cherry blossom perfume. It's an unabashedly quaffable rosé that's perfect for entertaining year round. Drink now."
Wine 3: Rosé, South Africa, $15. Tasting note: "With its juicy, citrus, melon and strawberry aromas and flavors, this dry rosé is mouthwatering and a food winner. Good minerality, fresh fruity character and a spicy finish give it added appeal. Crisp and refreshing, with layers of complexity to give it character."
Wine 4: Rosé, Portugal, $15. Tasting note: "There is an attractive light sparkle to this off-dry rosé. It has strawberry fruit and a touch of acidity that balances the candied softness. Drink now."
Wine 5: Champagne Blend, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "This attractive, light-colored rosé is dry, but its richness, crushed strawberry flavor and textured acidity neatly combine to produce a crisp, yet full, wine. Ready to drink."

request: I need to buy a present for someone, and price is no object. Can you help me find a bottle from Chile that tastes like cherry and plum and feels creamy?
wines:
Wine 1: Red Blend, Chile, $90. Tasting note: "Clos Apalta, depending on your point of view, is arguably Chile's best wine. And this vintage is outstanding! Earth, minty spice, ripe berry, minerality and smoky aromas cover the bases. It's superbly structured, with a fine texture and depth. Tastes lush and complex, with blackberry, crème de cassis, fine herbs and tobacco. Finishes classy. Drink now through 2016."
Wine 2: Red Blend, Chile, $70. Tasting note: "Valdivieso's nonvintage mystery blend is always one of Chile's most curious wines, and #16 happens to be superb. An opening of rich black-cherry aromas tips towards spice cake with raisins. A lush, saturated palate holds delicious flavors of chocolaty black fruits, while on the finish a dark smokiness takes over. Drink now–2023."
Wine 3: Red Blend, Chile, $40. Tasting note: "This dark, concentrated blend of five grapes opens with spicy aromas of coffee, black fruits and toasty oak. If the palate is a touch firm, airing or more time in bottle will soothe that. Tar, spice, olive, herbs and black-fruit flavors are deep and seamless, backed by licorice and chocolate on the finish. Drink through 2023."
Wine 4: Carmenère, Chile, $50. Tasting note: "This superb Carmenère is lusty but intricate on the bouquet, with aromas of baked plum, blackberry, balsam wood, leather and horse hide. The palate shows a complex blend of high-voltage power and density; flavors of roasted blackberry, chocolate, pepper and root beer finish deep and oaky. Drink through 2020."
Wine 5: Red Blend, Chile, $75. Tasting note: "Clos Apalta continues to push the envelope for Chilean icon wines. It's always been a blend of four or five Bordeaux grapes, and the 2005 is every bit as structured, tight and ripe as any predecessor. There is an intense blanket of new oak that tastes of mint, cinnamon, sawdust and black licorice. When that subsides (maybe in another 12 months), expect racy and complex berry flavors, pinpoint tannins and preserving acidity. Hold for another two years; then drink through 2014."

request: I want to try a new red wine that is a little sweet and not too heavy, with some spices, and costs between 20 and 40 euros.
wines:
Wine 1: Port, Portugal, $40. Tasting note: "This is a superb blend of aged tawny Ports, blended to celebrate the company's 325th anniversary. Filled with rich fruit, it has great depth and spicy richness although it is also impressively fresh. Dried fruits and red plums are lifted with a hint of smoky wood and good acidity. Like any tawny Port, it is ready to drink."
Wine 2: Syrah, US, $35. Tasting note: "A seriously top of the heap California Syrah. This complex, interesting wine sings of black pepper and garrigue, fleshy in just-ripe cherry, leather and dark plum. From the mountainous Fenaughty Vineyard, always a good source, it finishes long and will age gorgeously if you can possibly wait to drink it; that pepper will mellow in interesting ways."
Wine 3: Syrah, US, $40. Tasting note: "This is possibly the most savory rendition of Syrah made on the Central Coast, each vintage as feral as the last. This bottling shows bloody lamb, crushed peppercorn, soy and barnyard elements on the nose. The palate is tense with tarry structure, revealing unusual kelp, stewed peppercorn, black miso and teriyaki flavors."
Wine 4: Red Blend, Italy, $27. Tasting note: "This stunning Chianti Classico has an intense perfume of violet, rose and iris, accented with scents of truffle and forest berry. The wildly delicious palate presents a core of juicy cherry layered with sweet pipe tobacco, mint and spice, with a hint of well-integrated oak. It has great energy, with vibrant acidity and bracing but refined tannins. Drink 2016–2025."
Wine 5: Pinot Noir, US, $40. Tasting note: "There's a wildland, coastal mountain taste to this wine, which brims with bone-dry, exotic, woodsy tastes of wild forest cherries, fennel, balsam, cola, volcanic minerals, raw beef and Asian spices, not to mention the sweet veneer of sandalwood. It's utterly distinct from other Pinots in its almost feral complexity, a wine that changes with every sniff and sip. Should develop through 2014. This is a great price for a Pinot Noir of this integrity and interest. Only 152 cases were produced, but it's worth the search."

request: Hi, can you help me find a bottle of wine that isn't too heavy and tastes like herbs?
wines:
Wine 1: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $18. Tasting note: "This is a smooth, impressively rich wine powered by silky tannins and ripe black fruits. The palate is intensely concentrated with a big, bold structure and a solid feel. It does need some aging, so drink from 2016."
Wine 2: Touriga Nacional, Portugal, $36. Tasting note: "Named after the barn owl (Tyto alba) that nests in the woods of the Lezirias estate, this has great tannins that give shape to the dense black fruits. With a powerful structure and so much of the Touriga Nacional perfumes, this is a wine for aging. Drink from 2018."
Wine 3: Touriga Nacional, Portugal, $36. Tasting note: "This 100% Touriga Nacional comes from the government-owned estate in the north of Tejo. Named after the barn owl that is found in the woods, the wine is structured with dense tannins as well as concentrated black fruits. It is balanced with its fruit and structure already working well together, but it will need time. Drink from 2019."
Wine 4: Fernão Pires, Portugal, $77. Tasting note: "This fine low-production wood-aged wine is almost Burgundian in its creamy richness. The toast is nicely judged giving a wine that has just enough acidity and has plenty of textured apple and grapefruit flavors. The wine is named after the year of the creation of the Companhia das Lezirias."
Wine 5: Castelão, Portugal, $18. Tasting note: "A serious and dense wine, this is rich and full of dark juicy fruit. It has plenty of structure of course, with its rich tannins and wood aging flavors right up front. The acidity is perfumed, underlining the ripe fruit. Drink this concentrated wine from 2018."

request: Hi, I am looking for a light red wine with some spices that feels smooth, for a birthday party, and I want to try something new for under 25 euros.
wines:
Wine 1: Pinot Noir, US, $34. Tasting note: "This offers light red fruits and a dusting of spices. It's modest and balanced, with proportionate tannins and a chocolate note from aging in French oak barrels. It's a light, pleasant, but nondescript wine."
Wine 2: Meritage, US, $25. Tasting note: "This wine is a solid, stylish Meritage with assertive red fruit, a black pepper backbone and plenty of structure for aging. A touch of oaked spice adds dimension. A good overall red to pair with hearty winter fare."
Wine 3: Zweigelt, Austria, price unknown. Tasting note: "A simple wine full of red cherry flavors on the nose and palate, with an enticing white pepper edge that makes it very refreshing. This could be chilled and is an ideal, lighter-style red for informal entertainment."
Wine 4: Red Blend, US, $13. Tasting note: "Easygoing and soft in texture, this medium-bodied red wine has fruity, jammy aromas and flavors, and blends in a little black pepper for interest."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $95. Tasting note: "This will impress red wine lovers with its sheer deliciousness. It offers waves of blackberry and blueberry jam, dark chocolate, anise and cedar wood flavors, leading to a long, spicy finish. It's a bit soft, which might limit ageability, but it is a lovely wine to drink over the next few years."

request: Can you recommend a popular sparkling wine to raise a glass at a wedding that tastes a little sweet with nuts and honey, costing between 20 and 40 euros?
wines:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, US, $11. Tasting note: "A sweet style of sparkling wine, with brisk acidity framing orange, lime, vanilla and honey flavors. Nice with wedding cake, at a good price."
Wine 2: Sparkling Blend, US, $27. Tasting note: "A beautifully drinkable rosé sparkling wine for opening now. It's soft and honeyed, with fine bubbles framing slightly sweet flavors of raspberries, cherries, brioche, vanilla and toast."
Wine 3: Sparkling Blend, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "A lightly sparkling wine, this is refreshing and softly sweet with notes of honey and delicate acidity. Because it is low alcohol, it makes a delicious apéritif or accompaniment to dessert."
Wine 4: Prosecco, Italy, $13. Tasting note: "Upfront and immediate fragrances of sweet honey and acacia flower make this extremely aromatic.   The wine is bursting with sweet fruit freshness, creamy foam and sweet peach pie. It's also one of the best priced sparklers we've seen this year."
Wine 5: Chenin Blanc, France, $15. Tasting note: "This is a honey and almond-flavored wine. With its light acidity and creamed-apple fruitiness, it is soft with a crisp edge. Drink this attractive sparkling wine now."
